samples.summary: Hook installs document-wide capture listeners that programmatically blur elements outside its own subtree; scoping relies solely on a data attribute
samples.evidence: `useCanvasFocusRelease()` registers `pointerdown`/`keydown`/`focusin` on `document` in the CAPTURE phase (toolbar-focus-release.ts:125-127) and then calls `releaseFocusToBody()` -> `document.activeElement.blur()` (menu-focus.ts:68-72). The only scoping is the static `[data-canvas-toolbar]` attribute check. Any element that later carries that attribute — including one rendered inside a modal/overlay surface — becomes subject to asynchronous, out-of-band focus removal from a listener owned by a different component. `isPointerDrivenTarget()` also arms the release on a pointerdown inside ANY `[role="dialog"]`/`[role="menu"]`/`[role="listbox"]` anywhere in the page (line 50-51), not just popups opened from the toolbar, so an interaction in an unrelated dialog (e.g. the Share dialog) can arm a later release. I could not construct a concrete exploit: the deferred check additionally requires `document.activeElement` to be a BUTTON/role=button that is a DOM descendant of the toolbar root (line 71-79), Radix menus/dialogs are portalled out of the toolbar (components/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx:38), and no security-relevant control (confirmation, auth, share-token field) renders inside a `[data-canvas-toolbar]` root. Reported as hardening only: constraining the listeners to the toolbar element (ref-scoped) rather than `document` would remove the ambient blur capability entirely.
